https://www.coventrytelegraph.net/news/c.text: Workers have completed the first four major concrete support walls for a new bridge at the A46 Stoneleigh Junction, marking a key milestone in the long-awaited improvement scheme. The large concrete support walls, known as wingwalls, are vital structures that will bear the weight of the new road and embankments leading onto the bridge. In July, approximately 225 cubic metres of concrete were poured across four locations to form the walls, which range between 7.7 and 9.5 metres in height. Following the successful completion of these initial four structures, construction teams have progressed to the next set of wingwalls. The temporary moulds used to shape the concrete have been reused, and steel reinforcement is currently being installed ahead of further concrete works scheduled throughout August. Once these support walls are finished, the project will advance into its next phase, which involves building up the structural foundations and road approaches that will connect to the new bridge. The latest activity marks another tangible step forward in the delivery of the A46 Stoneleigh Junction improvement scheme, which aims to improve traffic flow, increase capacity and support future economic growth across the region. Councillor Stephen Shaw, Warwickshire County Council's Portfolio Holder for Transport and Planning, said: "Residents rightly want to see progress on this project, and that's exactly what is happening on site. "The completion of these first four major support walls marks a significant step forward and shows the new bridge continuing to take shape. "As a key part of the wider A46 Stoneleigh Junction improvement scheme, this achievement paves the way for the next phase of construction, which is already underway. "While the project has faced challenges, our focus remains firmly on delivery. These latest developments demonstrate tangible progress on site and bring us closer to delivering the improvements that residents, businesses and road users have been waiting for." https://www.wsws.org/en/articles/2026/08.text: Menu Search Latest Profile English Contact | About | International Committee of the Fourth International ( ICFI ) Menu Search International Committee of the Fourth International ( ICFI ) Latest Profile Fourth International Socialist Equality Party IYSSE About the WSWS Contact Donate Opposition to the imprisonment of Bogdan Syrotiuk continued to build over the weekend, six days after a Ukrainian court gave the 27-year-old socialist 15 years in prison for calling for the unity of Ukrainian and Russian workers against the war. The petition demanding his release passed 6,000 signatures. Nearly 500 people in more than 40 countries on five continents have added their names since the verdict, and letters have gone straight to the judges in Pervomaisk from historians, doctors, teachers and retired workers, each demanding that the sentence be thrown out. Since Thursday the court has heard from a distinguished professor of history in Texas, a historian of Soviet agriculture in West Virginia, an anthropologist at the Research Centre of the Slovenian Academy of Sciences and Arts and a doctor writing from Sri Lanka. Letters came as well from a retired teacher in Australia, a reader who signed as a retired civil servant in Britain and others in France, Turkey and the United States. Victoria Bynum, distinguished professor of history emerita at Texas State University and author of The Free State of Jones , wrote: As a historian and Distinguished Professor Emeritus, I am outraged to learn that Ukrainian socialist Bogdan Syrotiuk has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for expressing his political views in historical critiques published by the World Socialist Web Site. I implore the Pervomaisk City District Court to reverse this sentence and grant Mr. Syrotiuk his due rights of free speech. Mark B. Tauger, professor emeritus of history at West Virginia University and a historian of Soviet agriculture, wrote that Bogdan “did nothing wrong by expressing opposition to the insane Russian-Ukrainian war,” and that sentencing him “is first of all a gross violation of his civil rights and human rights.” “As many previous people have commented, this action resembles Russia’s suppression of opponents of the war, which makes me have second thoughts about supporting Ukraine in this conflict,” Tauger wrote. “...Syrotiuk’s views reflect those of many Ukrainians, and they should not be suppressed and he should not be imprisoned for expressing them.” Miha Kozorog, senior research associate at the Institute of Slovenian Ethnology of the Research Centre of the Slovenian Academy of Sciences and Arts and associate professor of anthropology at the University of Ljubljana, wrote: It is with concern and anger that I am following the erosion of democracy in Ukraine, and the verdict against Bogdan Syrotiuk—which I am monitoring through the Committee to Free Bogdan—is a major nail in the coffin of democracy and further proof to the world of what sort of country Ukraine is becoming. As a fellow human being, I implore you: overturn the verdict and set Bogdan free. K.T. Dhammika, who wrote to the court on Saturday as a medical doctor at Kandy Hospital in Sri Lanka, said the order to destroy Bogdan’s socialist books, leaflets and documents “reveals the political character of this verdict. These are the methods of fascism, not of a state that claims to be defending democracy.” He added: As a physician, I regard the deliberate withholding of medical treatment from a prisoner as a grave violation of human rights and a direct threat to his life. A 15-year sentence under such conditions amounts to a death sentence. Ukraine’s security service arrested Bogdan on April 25, 2024, and has held him ever since—more than 27 months. For over a year the prison has withheld the treatment his condition requires. No spying and no sabotage were shown at trial. What the state entered in evidence were his articles—which oppose Putin’s invasion and the NATO powers arming Kiev alike, and call on the workers of both countries to unite against the war—and the messages Bogdan exchanged with the editors who printed them. Adnan Çelik, writing from Turkey in both Ukrainian and English, pointed the court to its own repeated invocation of the “socially dangerous consequences” of Bogdan’s views and wrote: “This reveals that the prosecution against Bogdan is not related to the issue of support for Russia, which is a fabricated pretext.” He asked the court to quash the sentence and free Bogdan, to have the European Court of Human Rights take up the case without delay and to release every political prisoner in Ukraine’s jails. Tim Pearson wrote to the court: “The state’s experts examined 14 of Bogdan’s writings and included seven in the indictment. The court was then forced to drop one of the seven—an article on the military commissariats’ violent seizure of draft dodgers—after its own forensic commission could find nothing criminal in it. Therefore, Bogdan has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for writing six articles.” Riley Ward, writing from Michigan, quoted Article 34 of Ukraine’s own constitution—”Everyone is guaranteed the right to freedom of thought and speech, and to the free expression of his or her views and beliefs”—and added: “To be clear, I do not support the Putin regime or its reactionary invasion. The war... needs to end, but only workers uniting across borders will bring this about.” Frank Gaglioti, a retired teacher in Australia, wrote that “the prisons are full of Zelensky and his regimes opponents’ who are living under the most barbaric conditions. As Bogdan is very unwell, his sentence amounts to subjecting him to conditions of torture where he is being denied the most basic health care.” The petition drew the signature Saturday of Grzegorz Rossoliński-Liebe, the Berlin historian whose 2014 biography, Stepan Bandera: The Life and Afterlife of a Ukrainian Nationalist , traces the wartime collaborator’s transformation into a Ukrainian national hero. The verdict counts “reinterpretation of national heroes and historical figures” among Bogdan’s offenses. Jeremy Kuzmarov, managing editor of CovertAction Magazine, who reported Bogdan’s arrest in May 2024, signed Friday. Roger Waters, the co-founder of Pink Floyd, signed again on Saturday, writing “Free Bogdan.” Socialism AI by the WSWS SocialismAI.com Questions about this article? Ask Socialism AI What is the historical relationship between the ICFI and the WSWS, and why does the ICFI treat internationalist opposition to war as its central political program? Can you explain who Stepan Bandera was and why his rehabilitation as a national hero in Ukraine is politically significant today? How does Bogdan Syrotiuk's case compare historically to the persecution of anti-war socialists in other countries, like Karl Liebknecht during World War I? Ask more questions at SocialismAI.com A signer from Russia wrote Sunday, in Russian: “Bogdan Syrotiuk said only what the majority of Ukrainians think. For that he got 15 years in prison. And this is called democracy in Ukraine?” “Having a different opinion about things than your government is not treason,” wrote Cezar Turcanu of Romania on Sunday, one of 18 signatures from that country since the verdict. Signatures since the verdict came in the largest numbers from the United States, Britain, Australia, Germany and Canada, then Romania, Italy, Sri Lanka, Ireland, New Zealand and France. Smaller numbers came from 30 other countries, among them Ukraine, Russia, China, India, Turkey, Brazil, Peru and the Philippines. The German daily Junge Welt reported the sentence Saturday under the headline “Hochverrat unter Kriegsrecht”—”High treason under martial law.” On Sunday the Hungarian left-wing news site Pólus published an article headlined “Gondolatbűn Ukrajnában,” “Thought crime in Ukraine,” and the Russian-language independent site SVTV reported the case the same day. The journalist Aaron Maté, who hosts Pushback on the Grayzone, wrote on X Saturday: “Both Russia and Ukraine have persecuted anti-war activists. Boris Kagarlitsky, one of Russia’s top leftist intellectuals, is serving a five-year sentence for criticizing the invasion of Ukraine. Kyiv’s crackdown on Ukrainian dissidents gets far less Western attention. Ukrainian socialist Bogdan Syrotiuk has just been sentenced to 15 years in prison for ‘high treason’ for writing six articles in @WSWS_Updates critical of the Zelensky government.” As of Sunday, neither Reuters, the Associated Press, Agence France-Presse, CNN, the BBC, the Washington Post nor the New York Times had published a word on the case. Neither had Amnesty International, Human Rights Watch, Reporters Without Borders, the Committee to Protect Journalists nor PEN International. On RT Friday, the Russian state broadcaster’s international audience heard the case argued by Johannes Stern, who edits the World Socialist Web Site’s German edition. Bogdan, he said , had been “convicted for socialist thoughts, for an internationalist position opposing the war.” Bogdan’s lawyers must file their appeal within 30 days of the August 10 ruling, and the European Court of Human Rights has had a complaint over his detention before it since the spring of 2025. Every letter to the court and every signature on the petition strengthens that appeal. The World Socialist Web Site urges its readers—in workplaces, on campuses, in newsrooms, laboratories and studios—to add their names at wsws.org/freebogdan, to circulate the petition. Write to the Pervomaisk City District Court at inbox@pm.mk.court.gov.ua and the Mykolaiv Court of Appeal at inbox@mka.court.gov.ua, with a copy to freebogdan@wsws.org, demanding that the sentence be thrown out and Bogdan freed at once. http://www.euronews.com/2026/09/05/at-le.text: At least two people were killed and 81 were injured following two blasts at an army base in Bolivia on Friday, authorities said.Bolivian Defence Minister Ernesto Justiniano said the powerful explosions occurred at the RAM-2 “Bolívar” General Maintenance Center in Viacha, southwest of the administrative capital La Paz.According to Justiniano, the site was used to store "pyrotechnic material." He added that "no weaponry of any kind was detonated" during the incident."The most important thing tonight is to protect people, attend to the injured, continue the search for those who have not yet been located, and ensure that families can return to their homes only when conditions are safe,” he told reporters, adding that seven people remained missing.Footage circulating on social media appearing to capture one of the blasts shows a huge explosion and plume of smoke rising into the air.Justiniano said preliminary information showed the first explosion "involved black powder from pyrotechnic material stored at the site," while the second, "much larger" blast was still being investigated.In a post on X, Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz expressed his "deepest sympathy" with the families of the victims and those injured in the explosions."I have also ordered a thorough, technical, and transparent investigation into what happened," he wrote. "We must establish with absolute clarity the causes of this incident, verify compliance with safety protocols, and determine who is responsible".

https://www.politico.eu/article/france-c.text: BRUSSELS — France said new EU-wide taxes should generate over €60 billion toward the bloc's next seven-year budget , according to three EU diplomats, granted anonymity to about closed-door talks. Paris has emerged as the main supporter of new levies, known as own resources, insisting they will generate more revenue to spend on EU priorities such as defense and competitiveness, and reduce national contributions to Brussels. Securing Paris’ backing is crucial to obtain agreement among governments on a budget proposal by the end of the year, before elections in France, Italy, Poland and Spain in 2027 threaten to derail the talks. Advertisement Advertisement There are lingering concerns that a bad budget deal for France could boost the far-right National Rally, which is ahead in the polls and has campaigned to halve Paris’ contributions to the EU budget. During a closed-door discussion on Tuesday, France’s ambassador to the EU, Philippe Léglise-Costa, told colleagues that new EU-wide levies should generate over €60 billion — a high threshold for most other countries, according to the diplomats, who have direct knowledge of the talks. None of the other countries specified how much money they want to generate through the new taxes. While most governments support introducing new own resources, they have misgivings about the specific ideas on the table. The European Commission’s proposal from last July envisaged five new levies that would generate up to €66 billion in extra revenue. But the package has been met with resistance from national governments. The Irish Council presidency, which is steering discussions on the next Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), aims to narrow down the number of own resources that are acceptable for EU countries during a leaders’ summit in Brussels on Oct. 15. Dublin on Monday hailed “consensus” among governments to introduce new levies on foreign polluters, known as the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), and electronic waste that could respectively generate €1.64 billion and €17.9 billion per year on average from 2028 to 2034. During Tuesday's discussion, the Commission opened the door to tweaking some of the tax proposals to generate more revenue than initially foreseen, one of the diplomats said. But in a significant blow for France, other tax proposals — targeting tobacco products, corporate turnover and revenues from the Emissions Trading Scheme — have faced opposition from several countries, according to a note from Ireland seen by POLITICO. http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27928.text: Big News Network.com Tate brothers indicted in Romania over sex crimes involving minors Andrew and Tristan, currently in US custody, are also fighting a separate British extradition request over dozens of similar charges Romanian authorities have indicted social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate in absentia on charges including human trafficking, sex offenses involving minors, money laundering and witness tampering. The brothers have been held in a US jail since mid-July while fighting a separate British extradition request. Both have strongly denied wrongdoing. Andrew Tate, a former professional kickboxer and dual British-US citizen, built a global following promoting wealth, hyper-masculinity and traditional gender roles. His online content has attracted millions of followers while drawing widespread criticism over remarks about women. Romania's Directorate for the Investigation of Organized Crime and Terrorism (DIICOT) announced on Friday that Andrew had been charged with human trafficking, having sex with a minor, money laundering and influencing witnesses. Tristan is accused of aiding and abetting him. Prosecutors allege that in 2012 Andrew recruited a 15-year-old girl in the UK by falsely claiming he wanted a romantic relationship with her before taking her to Romania. She was then allegedly forced to produce pornographic content for a webcam business, with the brothers controlling her through threats, emotional blackmail and physical violence. Tristan allegedly managed proceeds from the operation totaling around $1.25 million. DIICOT is seeking the confiscation of four luxury cars allegedly bought with the money and registered in the names of associates. Prosecutors have separately accused Andrew of having sex with another 15-year-old girl. The case has been referred to the Bucharest Tribunal, where preliminary proceedings are expected to take at least two months. Eugen Vidineac, the brothers' Romanian lawyer, said the defense would challenge the indictment. Andrew and Tristan, who moved to Romania in 2016, were arrested there in December 2022 in a separate case involving similar allegations. An appeals court later returned that case to prosecutors after finding some evidence inadmissible. The charges were not dismissed, but travel restrictions were lifted in February 2025, allowing the brothers to fly to Florida. In July, Britain's Crown Prosecution Service announced additional charges against the Tates, bringing the British case to seven alleged victims and 59 charges combined, including rape, sexual assault and trafficking-related offenses. The brothers were subsequently arrested in Florida following a British extradition request. Their lawyer, Joseph McBride, has said Andrew and Tristan will vigorously fight extradition, describing the British case as politically motivated because his clients have repeatedly criticized the UK authorities and political establishment. http://www.jpost.com/influencers-26/50je.text: At a time when New York's Jewish community is navigating rising antisemitism and an increasingly polarized political landscape, Jessica Tisch and Julie Menin occupy two of the city's most powerful positions: one overseeing its police force, the other its City Council.Jessica TischTisch, the New York Police Department commissioner, and Menin, the first Jewish speaker of the New York City Council, are both prominent Jewish figures in a city with one of the largest Jewish populations outside Israel. Their influence has become particularly significant as concerns over Jewish safety have moved to the center of New York's political debate.Tisch became the second woman to lead the NYPD in November 2024. Protecting Jewish New Yorkers has been a visible feature of her tenure. The NYPD has mounted extensive security operations around major Jewish events, including the annual Israel Day Parade, while Tisch has repeatedly spoken publicly about the threat posed by antisemitism.A longtime member of Manhattan's Central Synagogue, Tisch addressed the congregation following an August attack during a Shabbat service, describing herself as a “proud Jew” with a “deeply personal” commitment to keeping her community safe. Earlier this year, she installed a mezuzah on her office at NYPD headquarters, calling it a symbol of “faith and resilience.”Julie Menin Menin, meanwhile, made history in January when she was unanimously elected the first Jewish speaker of the City Council. A veteran of New York government and a centrist Democrat, she has emerged as an important Jewish voice in the city's new political landscape, particularly following the election of Mayor Zohran Mamdani.Menin's own Jewish history has shaped her politics. Her mother and grandmother survived the Holocaust in Budapest, while her grandfather was murdered. She has on many occasions emphasized the importance of confronting antisemitism and preserving Holocaust memory, while seeking to maintain political dialogue across an increasingly divided New York.Together, Tisch and Menin represent two very different forms of Jewish power in New York: one through law enforcement and public safety, the other through political leadership. At a moment when Jewish New Yorkers are asking whether they can continue to live openly and confidently in the city, both have become increasingly important figures in answering that question.<< No. 11: Larry FinkNo. 13: Stephen Miller >>The 50 Most Influential Jews 2026 Full List
